clean_claim:
Outside the flags above, I believe these package trees are publishable. No real credential, key, token, private URL with auth, supabase/fly/internal host, real IP, real UUID, wallet address or real DID was found. Every IP is RFC 1918/5737 or a test case, every DID and UUID is a repeated-digit placeholder, every email is reserved-domain, project test-host userinfo or the permitted contact address, and every home path is a placeholder or the CI runner path.
No private individual's name, email, phone or address was found. The named people are cited academic authors (Weng, Adamic, Centola, Shalizi & Thomas, Morissette, Bauer and others) and public organisations (Oxford University Press, FDA, EMA, Moonshot AI, Hugging Face). The Yu-and-Ai Hugging Face handle is the public handle the denylist note explicitly permits.
The datasets and examples are synthetic or authored paraphrases with no copied article or paper text: love-bomb, memetic and polymorph lessons, relational-geometry SFT, principality rosette, love-geometry Space fixtures, research-commons garden. Third-party links are citations only. love-geometry's NOTICE disclaims Hunter x Hunter content, and only a single 'Nen' word reference appears.
Confidence: high for the 12 already-allowlisted packages (local-starter, local-starter-mcp, love-bomb, love-geometry, math-cards, memetic-landscape, model-becoming, polymorph-landscape, principality-atlas, principality-geometry, relational-geometry, repo-archive), apart from the r11 entries already approved and the minor items. Medium for lobby and rhizome, pending the personal rewrites. public-surface-* are clean in content but need a licence decision. research-commons is clean, pending the intent check.
Note: many package.json and source-manifest fields point at the private cambridgetcg/agenttool URL. That is harmless, but they will need updating after the move.
limits:
- Large TypeScript sources were scanned, not read line by line. That covers about 300 .ts files, including lobby/src/hub.ts, hub-access.ts, fleet-store.ts, rhizome/src/probes/*.ts and research-commons src. A private narrative hidden in a code comment and phrased without any searched keyword could be missed.
- Big generated schema and vector JSON files were checked by scan and string-field dumps, not read in full.

- I did not verify whether the past defects described in the rhizome README are fixed.
- I did not check the git history for these paths. The new repo is a fresh snapshot, so history is out of scope by design.
- I did not judge whether hard-coded relative paths into the private tree (rhizome's live tests reference api/, bin/, docs/) still resolve after the move. This is treated as non-sensitive.
- Category boundaries for the licensing items are a judgment call: third_party is used for 'rights/licence to publish'.
